the end-Triasic and Early Jurassic events are recorded in an integrated stratigraphic framework at Csővár (Hungary), a new section studied in detail.
the end-Triasic extinction event and the associated δ13Ccarbon excursion are not a single event, but a series of short-term perturbances that are not linked to sea-level change.

the Triassic– Jurassic transition was marked by a short-term climatic warming, followed by an episode of rapid global warming and a negative δ13 Ccarb excursion.

the Triassic– Jurassic boundary interval was characterized by a rapid and pronounced warming, which caused the extinction of benthic foraminifers, conodonts and radiolarians.
